Hon'ble Vinod Diwakar,J. 
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused material on record.

2. The instant application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to quash the cognizance order dated 15.09.2021, passed by the Civil Judge (J.D.)/Judicial Magistrate, Gunnaur, Sambhal,
charge-sheet no. 99 of 2020 dated 17.03.2020 as well as entire proceedings of Case No. 1147 of 2021, titled State v. Dr. Sanjeev Kumar, arising out of Case Crime No. 40 of 2020, under Section 420 IPC and Section 15(2), 15(3) of Indian Medical Council Act, P.S. Rajpura, District Sambhal.
3.

The facts of the case in brief is that on 14.01.2020 at around 4.00 P.M. a raid was conducted by Dr. Manoj Kumar, posted as Quacks Nodal Officer, District Hospital, District Sambhal, at Dr. Sunil's clinic situated at Shergarh Hasanpur, District Amroha and seized certain incriminating documents.

During raid, it was reveled that the clinic was run by a quack without having any medical Dr Sanjeev Kumar Mishra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33539959/
1 qualification in contravention of Section 15(2), 15(3) of Indian Medical Council Act read with Section 420 IPC at the behest of Dr. Sanjeev Kumar Mishra, who was posted at Community Health Center, Islam Nagar (Rudayan) District Budaun.
4.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the instant FIR has been registered by police at behest of Health Department with ulterior motive.
The police did not follow the procedure as established under law while conducting the proceedings of the seizure.
Learned counsel has relied upon the seizure conducted by the police, which is forming part of charge-sheet, wherein one Sunil shown working in the clinic.

5. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the application and submitted that it has come in the investigation that actually the clinic in question was being run by the applicant and it's not relevant at this stage whether the applicant was present on the clinic at the time of inspection or not.

Further,
in investigation, it's revealed that clinic was being operated by Dr Sanjeev Kumar Mishra, applicant herein.
6. In the instant matter, the submissions raised by learned counsel for the applicant call for determination on questions of fact which may be adequately adjudicated upon only by the trial court.
Adjudication of questions of facts and appreciation of evidence or examining the reliability and credibility of the version, does not fall within the arena of jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

In view of the material on record it can also not be held that the impugned criminal proceeding are manifestly attended with mala fide and maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge.

Similarly no such illegality, perversity or any other substantial error could be pointed out in the impugned summoning order, so as to warrant any interference by this court in exercise of powers u/s 482 Cr.P.C.
7.

Perusal of the contents of FIR and the statement of witnesses and informant recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., it's prima-facie established that the applicant was running a clinic through a quack without having any medical qualification in contravention of Section 15(2), 15(3) of Indian Medical Council Act read with Section 420 IPC, and was actually involved in day to day affairs of the clinic in question, therefore, no case for quashing of impugned proceedings is made out.
8. The application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is devoid of merit and it is accordingly dismissed.
